claims.text: Temperature ramp rate, dwell time, and applied pressure are SPS variables that can be adjusted to control the resulting microstructure.
Machine-learning-guided optimization of those SPS variables will produce a more uniform W–Cu microstructure.
Machine-learning-guided SPS optimization will minimize voids in vapor-coated W–Cu composites.
Machine-learning-guided SPS optimization will improve bonding at W–Cu interfaces.
Improved W–Cu interfacial contact and reduced void content will enhance thermal transport.
The optimized material will maintain or improve mechanical durability under fusion-relevant irradiation and thermal loading.
Existing vapor-coating and SPS methods produce vapor-coated W particles or connected W regions embedded in a Cu matrix.
The SPS process will be conducted under a controlled inert atmosphere with monitored heating and pressure profiles.
The ML framework will analyze in situ sensor data and historical experimental outcomes to predict an optimal SPS cycle.
The predicted optimal SPS cycle will eliminate thermal gradients and uneven pressure distributions.
Eliminating thermal gradients and uneven pressure distributions will cause uniform densification and enhanced W–Cu interfacial bonding.
The optimized cycle will prevent phase separation and void nucleation.
Relative to conventional SPS, the optimized composite will have a statistically significant reduction in void density.
Relative to conventional SPS, the optimized composite will have higher thermal conductivity.
Vapor-coated W powders consolidated by a non-optimized SPS cycle constitute the current standard fabrication baseline.
The claimed benefits are restricted initially to laboratory-scale SPS processing and must persist under fusion-joint thermal and irradiation loads.
The optimal SPS parameter window may vary with batch-to-batch powder quality.
Scaling ML-guided SPS from laboratory to industrial production may introduce additional challenges.
A controlled comparison of conventional and ML-optimized SPS specimens followed by identical thermal and irradiation exposure can test the hypothesis.
Failure to improve all listed microstructural and performance outcomes relative to the baseline will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The experiment specifies a conventional SPS cycle for one group and an ML-optimized SPS cycle for the other, but then says both groups will be subjected to identical sintering procedures. The sintering cycles cannot be both different and identical; only downstream service exposures should be identical.
